in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name 'Prætextus' was derived from the word 'prætextus', meaning pretender or cover, possibly due to its use in the Latin phrase 'prætextus verbum Dei', meaning 'the word of God covered or veiled'.

in_english.name: Prent
in_english.long_meaning: The English name 'Prent' is derived from the Old English word 'prentan', meaning 'to serve', which in turn is derived from the Proto-Germanic word 'prei-entan', meaning 'young man' or 'apprentice'. In Middle English, 'prent' also came to mean a servant or a laborer. This name was often given to young men who were starting their careers or apprenticeships.
